title: Camera shots and angles
examples: What is the difference between a wide shot and a medium shot?
When should a director use a low angle?
Can a camera angle change how we feel about a character?

explain.say: Today we are learning about camera shots and angles.

items: Wide Shot: Shows setting and action
Medium Shot: Shows character from waist up
Close-up: Focuses on face or small object

explain.say: A wide shot shows the character and their surroundings clearly.
A medium shot shows a character from about the waist up.
A close-up shot focuses tightly on a person's face or an object.
A high angle shot looks down at the subject from above.
A low angle shot looks up at the subject from a low position.

faq.q: What is the main difference between a wide shot and a medium shot?
faq.a: The wide shot shows more of the background and setting around the character. The medium shot cuts in closer, usually showing the character from the waist up.
asks: How far back is a wide shot?
Can you show me the difference between wide and medium?

faq.q: When should a director use a low angle shot?
faq.a: Directors often use a low angle to make a character appear powerful or important. It makes the subject seem larger than life.
asks: Does a low angle make people look strong?
Why would you film someone from below?

faq.q: Does the camera angle change how we feel about the character?
faq.a: Yes, the angle affects the audience's perception of the character. For example, a high angle can make them seem small or weak.
asks: What emotion does a high angle create?
Can the camera angle trick the viewer?

faq.q: Is a close-up only for faces?
faq.a: No, a close-up can focus on any small detail, like a character's hands or an important object. It draws the viewer's attention to that specific detail.
asks: Can I use a close-up on something other than a person?
What is the purpose of a close-up shot?

faq.q: What is the best shot to show an action happening in a large area?
faq.a: You should use a wide shot for this. It gives the audience a sense of the scale and the environment where the action takes place.
asks: Which shot shows the most background?
If I need to show a big fight, what shot do I use?

facts: A wide shot establishes the setting and context for the scene.
A low angle shot generally makes the subject look more powerful or dominant.
A close-up shot emphasizes emotion or detail by filling the frame.
A high angle shot can make a character appear vulnerable or small.

quiz.say: If a director wants the audience to feel that a character is very powerful, which angle should they use?
quiz.why: A low angle shot forces the viewer to look up, making the subject appear larger and more imposing.

wrong.0: A wide shot shows the environment, not necessarily the character's perceived power.
wrong.1: A medium shot is balanced and doesn't exaggerate the character's size.
wrong.2: A high angle makes the subject look smaller or less powerful.

quiz.say: To show a character's subtle facial reaction, which shot is most effective?
quiz.why: The close-up eliminates distractions and forces the audience to focus entirely on facial expressions.

wrong.1: A wide shot would show too much background, distracting from the face.
wrong.2: A medium shot includes the body, which takes focus away from the face.
wrong.3: The angle changes the perception of the face, but the close-up is best for detail.

quiz.say: A shot that shows a character and a lot of their surrounding environment is called:
quiz.why: The wide shot is designed specifically to establish the setting and show the character within it.

wrong.0: A medium shot only shows the character from the waist up, leaving out much of the setting.
wrong.1: The angle changes the view, but the wide shot describes the scope of the shot.
wrong.3: A close-up zooms in too much and leaves out the surroundings.
